mode: Native MySQL view creation in persistent named schemas, utf8mb4 connection, empty sql_mode and case-sensitive database and relation names.

CreateView.role: A complete persistent MySQL view declaration with its creation and execution policies.
CreateView.structure: An absolute view identity, resolved result heading, checked SELECT body, creation policy, algorithm and SQL security mode. An optional resolved native view check policy. A resolved session definer rule or a named account identity.
CreateView.conditions: Require an unbounded checked plain or DISTINCT projection from one persistent base relation or independent literals. Check all existing heading, identity, scope, parameter, and policy boundaries. A check policy requires a mergeable base-table projection. MySQL 5.6 and 5.7 admit an all-constant base projection with a check option. Later profiles require a projected writable base field when a check option is present.
CreateView.meaning: Create, replace or preserve the named view under the stored policy. The native view reuses the resolved query and exposes its explicitly indicated result names and native field order. The default definer is the executing account. A named definer supplies the exact account identity. SQL SECURITY specifies the effective privilege context for view use. Its requested directive remains fixed. The installed algorithm is derivable from the body and the directive if a new definition takes effect. The check policy controls whether inserts or updates through the view must satisfy its predicate.
CreateView.sql: Emit the exact absolute target with the resulting column list, creation option, algorithm, security and closed SELECT. Generate distinct internal query labels inside the ordered heading. Write the canonical native CHECK OPTION for the resolved policy.

ViewColumn.role: A name in the catalog heading of a persistent MySQL view.
ViewColumn.structure: One checked identifier for the resulting position.
ViewColumn.conditions: This domain admits one through 64 non-NUL ASCII characters without a trailing space. Compare heading names with ASCII case folding and reject duplicates in the owner.
ViewColumn.meaning: Name this exact catalog position for future qualification or wildcard expansion.
ViewColumn.sql: Quote the decoded identifier in the explicit heading list.

ViewCreationPolicy.structure: Require new, replace a view, or preserve an existing name.
ViewCreationPolicy.conditions: The modes are mutually exclusive. The checked preserve mode is available on the MySQL 9.1.0 pin.
ViewCreationPolicy.meaning: Respect the native existing-object outcome of the selected creation statement.
ViewCreationPolicy.sql: Emit ordinary CREATE VIEW, CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW, or CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS.

ViewAlgorithm.role: The requested native view evaluation algorithm and its installed interpretation.
ViewAlgorithm.conditions: All three algorithm requests may be used with checked plain or DISTINCT projections over a persistent base table or independent literals.
ViewAlgorithm.meaning: A requested MERGE over an independent or DISTINCT projection emits warning 1354 and installs UNDEFINED on successful creation. The diagnostic is ordered before a same-name collision warning or error. A distinct body always materializes.
ViewAlgorithm.sql: Emit the requested algorithm. The server performs the effective algorithm fallback and reports its native warning.

ViewSecurity.role: The native execution security context of the view.
ViewSecurity.conditions: The input selects one mode and uses the implicit definer of the creation execution.
ViewSecurity.meaning: Evaluate the view under the privileges of the definer or invoker as declared.
ViewSecurity.sql: Emit the matching SQL SECURITY clause and leave the native implicit definer selection intact.

ViewCheckOption.role: The native rule for a new row written through an installed view.
ViewCheckOption.conditions: Require a base source with a mergeable query and an algorithm that permits merging. MySQL 5.6 and 5.7 admit an all-constant base projection with a check option. Later profiles require a projected writable base field when a check option is present. A legacy all-constant view still has a nonupdatable catalog flag. A filter is optional. Unqualified WITH CHECK OPTION denotes CASCADED.
ViewCheckOption.meaning: Without a check option, a write through the view can install rows that the view does not display. With a check option, the view predicate must be TRUE for a new row image. FALSE and UNKNOWN cause native check error 1369 and preserve the underlying data. LOCAL and CASCADED enforce the same predicate over a base table but have independently visible catalog modes.
ViewCheckOption.sql: Omit the clause for None. Emit WITH LOCAL CHECK OPTION or WITH CASCADED CHECK OPTION for the corresponding modes.

ViewDefiner.role: An explicit MySQL account identity assigned to a persistent view.
ViewDefiner.structure: Two distinct decoded UTF-8 fields. User spelling is case-sensitive. Host spelling uses the native simple lowercase normalization.
ViewDefiner.conditions: Decode both account components and remove ASCII space, tab, carriage return, newline, vertical tab and form feed from their edges. Interior bytes and non-ASCII whitespace remain significant. The owner checks the release-specific width of the canonical account. Authored two-part names in MySQL 5.6 and 5.7 must also fit the native limits before trimming or folding. MySQL 8.0 and later check the trimmed host bytes before folding.
ViewDefiner.meaning: Record the two-part account identity independently of account existence and grants. The requested SQL SECURITY mode chooses execution under the definer or invoker. Account availability and privileges are external and produce native effects, including diagnostics.
ViewDefiner.sql: Emit DEFINER with each component quoted separately. Preserve delimiters, escape characters, and UTF-8 text as data. Normalize CURRENT_USER and CURRENT_USER() clauses to the session definer rule.

structure: A checked persistent declaration retains the query and exact result positions. Every external reference is absolute. The definition includes explicit policy values and an effective heading independent of the source spelling.
conditions: Admit checked ordinary unbounded projections over a resolved persistent base table or independent literals, with explicit ALL or DISTINCT semantics and all three algorithm requests. Retain all previously checked exclusions and boundaries. Accept each native check mode over a mergeable direct base projection. Reject check policies for independent, DISTINCT, and TEMPTABLE queries. MySQL 5.6 and 5.7 admit an all-constant base projection with a check option. Later profiles require a projected writable base field when a check option is present.
meaning: The declaration creates a server view with an explicit result heading and uses the body when read. Preserve data multiplicity and NULL over future changes to the input. Retain native catalog behavior for existing objects, algorithm, security and implicit commit. View writes preserve the catalogued check policy and the exact native accept, reject, and row-change effects.
sql: Render the definition from the scoped SELECT and exact heading, with stable quoting and no stored SQL fragment. Normalize omitted algorithm and security to their native defaults. Use the native DUAL singleton for the earlier releases when an isolated projection needs a FROM clause. The view body requires no subquery to supply that row. Normalize an unqualified CHECK OPTION to explicit CASCADED.

The native observer captures the ordered, typed view creation diagnostics, which also distinguish a requested MERGE from an already normalized UNDEFINED.
The independent effect evaluator applies the resolved predicate to the candidate new row image using three-valued SQL truth. Both native executions use the fixed authorized disposable fixture.
The native 5.6 calibration distinguishes admission and the installed IS_UPDATABLE flag for a base projection of constants.
Definer access is observed independently with three disjoint grant-table identities and an authorized fixture creator. Access checks depend on the same external authorization state on both sides.

The native 8.0.44 rejection was found by comparing both authored SQL and emitted SQL. The 5.7 calibration independently confirms the legacy boundary.

checkFinite.completeness: Reconstruct the installed semantic check mode from the graph and the spelling discriminator from the actual frozen analyzed input. Check that unqualified and explicit CASCADED produce the same graph. Compare the complete independent coordinate sets separately for analysis and direct construction.

writeProbes.rule: Run the three inserts and the update in the given order through the installed policy fixture. Compare each effect to the independent base-row evaluator. The bounded write fixture uses distinct id and label columns, signed id and exact text, duplicated id and label pairs, and SQL NULL. The placement checks are independent of those values.

checkCatalogFinite.observation: Compare creation effect, ordered native fields, duplicate multiplicity, catalog check and updatability. The write probe domain uses the two distinct writable fields defined under writeProbes.

rejections.policy: Retain the original analyzed and direct coordinates. Each rejected coordinate requires a typed PHP rejection and separate native rejection with no newly installed view.

definerFinite.fixture: Create an absent view over the same nonempty physical table in an isolated root session. The fixture includes duplicate and NULL rows. Only ir_def_reader@localhost is granted physical reads. Also create ir_def_reader@% and the case-distinct Ir_Def_Reader@localhost without that grant. Distinct absent named accounts remain absent. Check the root@% identity from CURRENT_USER at initialization.
definerFinite.completeness: Recover both source spellings and the normalized account fields from independently observed construction and fixture requests. Resolve every spelling to the individually specified canonical definer. Enumerate the independent product of algorithm, SQL security and supported account spelling per route.

widthWitnesses.scope: Observe maximum user width in characters and ASCII and multibyte host spellings under the relevant byte boundary. On legacy releases cover it as an explicit native and construction refusal and add the valid 60-byte multibyte host to the positive domain.

definerLimits.sourceWarnings: Observe native bounds with isolated server probes. Supplementary characters use a separate lossy-conversion rule that is open here.
definerLimits.hostRule: The user component is measured in BMP characters. The host component is measured in UTF-8 bytes and excludes ASCII @. Admission checks the host byte width for the enclosing release. The normalized host byte sequence must be writable under that release.

normalizationOrder.direct: Normalize the semantic account input by trimming edge ASCII whitespace. Validate the user character and host byte widths and host delimiter before host case folding in the general account role. The enclosing native release additionally checks its canonical account widths.
normalizationOrder.mysql-5.6.51: Before normalization, the authored two-part operation checks the original user character and host byte limits. For an authored user-only form the parser trims the user first.
normalizationOrder.mysql-5.7.44: Before normalization, the authored two-part operation checks the original user character and host byte limits. For an authored user-only form the parser trims the user first.
normalizationOrder.modern: After trimming edge ASCII whitespace, an authored account checks character and byte widths, then folds the host.

definerDiagnostic.rule: Limit each account component to 64 bytes in the English absent-account note. MySQL 5.6 and 5.7 emit the well-formed UTF-8 prefix, omitting a cut partial character. MySQL 8.0 and later display each retained byte of a cut character as a question mark. Preserve the complete catalog identity in both groups.
